mainTopic: Whether הוצאה includes bringing in, and whether the list of נגעים shades fits רבי עקיבא
overview: The גמרא first shows that a תנא can use the word הוצאה, 'carrying out,' even for bringing an item into a private domain. It proves this from the משנה 'המוציא מרשות לרשות חייב,' whose general wording covers both directions. It then explains why: any removal of an item from its place counts as הוצאה. רבינא adds support from the opening משנה of שבת, which calls all the cases יציאות but then lists cases of bringing in. רבא rejects that proof, because he reads that משנה as counting the two domains of שבת. The גמרא then turns to the next line of our משנה, the shades of נגעים, and quotes the משנה in נגעים listing four shades of white. רבי חנינא says that list does not follow רבי עקיבא, because under רבי עקיבא's ranking the lime shade could not combine with any other shade. The amud ends with a challenge: the egg membrane shade has the same problem, so why didn't רבי חנינא mention it too?

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: carrying from one domain to another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה 'המוציא מרשות לרשות חייב' and argues that it includes bringing in, yet still uses the word הוצאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who carries out from one domain to another domain is liable. Aren't we also dealing with a case where he is bringing an item in, and still the משנה calls it 'carrying out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that the word הוצאה can also mean bringing an item in. It points to a משנה that uses general wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'from one domain to another' without saying which direction. So it should include bringing in from public to private as well. Even so, the משנה uses the verb המוציא, 'carrying out.' That suggests the תנא calls הכנסה by the name הוצאה.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who carries out from domain to domain is liable.
Are we not dealing
with a case where he is actually bringing in –
and still it calls it 'carrying out'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier claim on this daf that הכנסה is also called הוצאה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a תנא calls bringing in by the name הוצאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת: המוציא מרשות לרשות חייב.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה only means carrying out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: maybe the משנה only means carrying out from private to public.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he is carrying out from a private domain to a public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 1. Maybe the משנה is only talking about real carrying out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה only means taking from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים, then המוציא simply means 'carrying out' in the normal sense. Then the משנה proves nothing about הכנסה.

phrases.english: But perhaps he is taking out
from a private domain to a public domain?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא קָא מַפֵּיק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה used in the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה includes bringing in.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה could be read narrowly as real carrying out only, so the word הוצאה would be used in its plain sense.

steps.title: The general wording must include bringing in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the proof: if the משנה meant only private to public, it would have said so. The general wording shows it includes public to private too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach: 'One who carries out from a private domain to a public domain.' What is 'from domain to domain'? That even from a public domain to a private domain is included, and still it calls it 'carrying out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 2 by looking closely at the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the משנה meant only private to public, it could easily have said that. Instead it chose the broad wording 'from domain to domain.' That broad wording must be there to include bringing in, and the משנה still uses the word הוצאה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's general wording 'מרשות לרשות' includes both directions, yet it is called הוצאה.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach:
'One who carries out from a private domain to a public domain';
What is 'from domain to domain'?
That even from a public domain to a private domain is included,
and still it calls it 'carrying out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נִיתְנֵי הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 and brings back the proof of Step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might mean only carrying from private to public.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general wording includes public to private, and the משנה still calls it הוצאה.

steps.title: Why call bringing in 'carrying out'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the תנא uses the word הוצאה for bringing in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why the תנא would use the word 'carrying out' for bringing something in. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It has been shown that the תנא does this. Now the גמרא wants to know the logic behind the word choice, since bringing in sounds like the opposite of carrying out.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the conclusion of Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנא calls bringing in by the name הוצאה.

steps.title: Any removal of an item from its place is called carrying out
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תנא calls any lifting of an item from its place הוצאה, whatever the direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא calls any removal of an item from its place 'carrying out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 4. For the תנא, 'carrying out' means taking the item out of its spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הוצאה is not about leaving the house. It is about the item being taken out of its place (עקירה). Since that happens in both directions, bringing in can also be called הוצאה.
steps.whatToRemember: For the תנא, הוצאה means taking an item out of its place (עקירת חפץ), so it covers bringing in as well.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read הוצאה here as only 'taking outside.' Here it means removing an item from where it was resting, in either direction.

phrases.english: The תנא, any removal of an item from its place –
calls it 'carrying out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא, כׇּל עֲקִירַת חֵפֶץ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוֹצָאָה קָרֵי לַהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא uses הוצאה for any removal of an item from its place, so it includes bringing in.

steps.title: רבינא: the opening משנה of שבת shows this too
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings support: the משנה calls everything יציאות שבת, yet it goes on to explain cases of bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The משנה is also precise, as it teaches: 'The carryings out of שבת are two that are four inside, and two that are four outside,' and then it explains cases of bringing in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a second proof for the same idea, from the wording of another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening משנה of שבת labels all the cases יציאות, 'carryings out.' But when it lists them, some are cases of bringing in. So the label 'carrying out' must include bringing in.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise, its wording shows this

phrases.english: רבינא said:
The משנה is also precise,
phrases.notes: He means the opening משנה of מסכת שבת, which uses the same wording.

phrases.english: as it teaches: 'The carryings out of שבת
are two that are four inside
and two that are four outside,'
and it goes on to explain bringing in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent proof for the idea of Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the term הוצאה / יציאות includes הכנסה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opening משנה of שבת: יציאות שבת שתים שהן ארבע, which then lists cases of הכנסה.

steps.title: Conclusion: carrying out includes bringing in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from רבינא's proof that the word for carrying out also covers bringing in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבינא's proof and closes this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is accepted. The term יציאות / הוצאה in a משנה can include bringing an item in.
steps.whatToRemember: A תנא may call both carrying out and bringing in by the name הוצאה, because both involve removing an item from its place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the משנה can call all the cases יציאות שבת, even though some of them are really cases of bringing in.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The term הוצאה / יציאות also includes הכנסה.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה is counting domains, not acts of carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבינא's proof. He says the משנה is counting the two domains of שבת, so its wording proves nothing about the word הוצאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the משנה is teaching about domains. There are two domains on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבינא's proof in Step 6. He reads the שבת משנה in a way that gives no proof that הוצאה includes bringing in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed the משנה was calling every case a 'carrying out'. רבא says 'שתים' counts the two domains, public and private, and moving between them in either direction gives the four cases. Read this way, the משנה never calls bringing in 'carrying out', so it is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The domains that matter for the laws of carrying on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'יציאות שבת שתים שהן ארבע'. רבינא reads it as calling bringing in 'carrying out'. רבא says the משנה is really counting the two domains of שבת, so it is no proof.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is teaching domains;
the domains of Shabbat are two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's proof from Steps 6-7 by reading the משנה as counting domains.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה uses the language of carrying out for cases of bringing in
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is not counting acts of carrying. It is counting the two domains of שבת.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of our משנה: shades of leprous marks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to the next phrase of our משנה: 'מראות נגעים שנים שהן ארבעה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה says: the shades of נגעים are two, which are really four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of our משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists several 'two that are four' cases. Now the גמרא turns to the case of נגעים, the skin marks of צרעת. It will explain this line by quoting the full משנה in מסכת נגעים.

phrases.english: The shades of leprous marks
are two that are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next phrase of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two main shades of נגעים, and each has a secondary shade, making four.

steps.title: The משנה in נגעים lists the four shades
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in נגעים: בהרת is white like snow and its secondary shade is like the lime of the היכל. שאת is like white wool and its secondary shade is like the skin inside an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: the shades of נגעים are two, which are four. בהרת is bright white like snow, and below it is a shade like the lime plaster of the היכל. שאת is like white wool, and below it is a shade like the skin of an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the full משנה from מסכת נגעים to explain which four shades our משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two' are the main marks named in the תורה, בהרת and שאת. The 'four' adds a lighter secondary shade to each one. The order of these shades will matter in the next step, where רבי חנינא asks which תנא this list follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white skin mark, one of the main types
A white skin mark like wool, the other main type
The lime plaster on the walls of the היכל
The thin skin just inside an eggshell

phrases.english: We learned there:
Shades of leprous marks are two that are four:
Baheret is intense white, like snow;
secondary to it is a shade like the lime of the Sanctuary.
Se'et is like white wool;
secondary to it is a shade like the membrane of an egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the line of our משנה by quoting the full source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four shades are: בהרת (snow) with its secondary shade סיד היכל, and שאת (wool) with its secondary shade קרום ביצה.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks who taught this list
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא asks which תנא is the author of the משנה about the shades of נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: who is the תנא who taught the משנה of the shades of נגעים?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא asks whose opinion the list of shades follows. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה pairs each main shade with its own secondary shade. רבי חנינא wants to know which opinion fits this way of grouping the shades.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (author) of this משנה?

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Who is the tanna who taught the shades of leprous marks?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאן תַּנָּא מַרְאוֹת נְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the author of the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion the list of shades follows

steps.title: The list does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that this משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers his own question: this משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not yet say who the author is. He only rules out רבי עקיבא. His reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with רבי עקיבא's opinion

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The author of the משנה is not רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why not רבי עקיבא: the lime shade could not combine
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא ranks each shade one above the next. If so, the shade of סיד היכל would be left unable to combine with another shade, so a mark of that shade would stay pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the author were רבי עקיבא, there is a problem. He says each shade is ranked one above the other. If so, you have made the lime shade pure, because it cannot combine with the others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא proves his claim. He shows that רבי עקיבא's ranking of the shades does not fit the way this משנה groups them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא puts all the shades in one ladder, from brightest to dimmest. In that order the lime shade does not sit next to its partner, בהרת, the way the משנה pairs them. So under his view a small mark of lime-white could not join with another shade to reach the needed size, and it would stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is above that one (a ranking of shades)
To combine (two shades joining to reach the needed size)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'טיהרת סיד היכל' as saying lime-white is never a נגע. The problem is only that it could not combine with another shade to reach the needed size.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא says the משנה of the four shades is not רבי עקיבא's, because his ranking would leave the סיד היכל shade unable to combine with the others.

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Akiva,
since he says:
this one is above this one,
and that one is above that one,
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא lines up all the shades in one order, from brightest to dimmest.

phrases.english: if so, you have rendered pure
the lime of the Sanctuary, so that it does not combine.
phrases.notes: He means a small lime-white mark could not join with another shade to reach the size that makes a person impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר: זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ וְזוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the answer in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה of the shades is not רבי עקיבא's
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's ranking 'זו למעלה מזו', which would leave סיד היכל unable to combine

steps.title: The lime shade has no partner to combine with
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי עקיבא, סיד היכל cannot join בהרת, because שאת sits between them. It also cannot join שאת, because it is not שאת's secondary shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: With which shade could we combine it? Should we combine it with בהרת? There is שאת, which is brighter than it. Should we combine it with שאת? It is not its secondary shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out step 13's claim. It tries each possible partner for the lime shade and shows that neither one works under רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's order is: snow (בהרת), wool (שאת), lime (סיד), egg membrane. בהרת cannot combine with lime because שאת stands between them, so they are not next to each other. שאת is right next to lime, but lime belongs to בהרת's family, not שאת's. So lime has no partner, and that clashes with the משנה, which lists it as a secondary shade that does combine.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us combine it, meaning count it together with another shade
Which is higher or brighter than it
A secondary shade, the 'offspring' of a main shade
The main נגע shade, white like snow
The second main נגע shade, white like wool

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that two shades sitting next to each other can always combine. Under רבי עקיבא they must be next to each other and also belong to the same family.

phrases.english: With which shade could we combine it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the lime shade of the היכל from step 13.

phrases.english: Should we combine it with בהרת?
There is שאת, which is brighter than it.
phrases.notes: שאת sits between snow and lime in רבי עקיבא's order, so בהרת and lime are not next to each other.

phrases.english: Should we combine it with שאת?
It is not its secondary shade.
phrases.notes: Lime is the secondary shade of בהרת, not of שאת (step 10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind step 13's claim that the lime shade would be left without a partner.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה about the shades of נגעים does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's ranking of the shades, combined with the rule that only a main shade and its own secondary shade combine

steps.title: Why not bring the same proof from the egg membrane shade?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי חנינא didn't also point to קרום ביצה, which seems stuck in the same way: שאת is not next to it, and סיד is not in its family.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the egg membrane shade too: with which shade could we combine it? Should we combine it with שאת? There is lime, which is brighter than it. Should we combine it with lime? It is not of its kind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's choice of proof. The egg membrane shade has the very same problem as lime, so why did he mention only lime?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Egg membrane is the secondary shade of שאת. Under רבי עקיבא's order, lime sits between wool and egg membrane, so שאת is not next to it. Lime is next to it but belongs to בהרת's family. So the egg membrane shade should also be left without a partner, and רבי חנינא could have cited it as a second proof.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a challenge built on what was just said
The skin inside an egg, the secondary shade of שאת
Lime, here the lime of the היכל, the secondary shade of בהרת
Of its kind, the same family

phrases.english: If so, the egg membrane shade too:
With which shade could we combine it?
Should we combine it with שאת?
There is lime, which is brighter than it.
phrases.notes: Lime sits between wool and egg membrane, so שאת and egg membrane are not next to each other.

phrases.english: Should we combine it with lime?
It is not of its kind!
phrases.notes: Lime belongs to בהרת's family and egg membrane belongs to שאת's family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 14 to ask why רבי חנינא did not apply it to the egg membrane shade as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's choice to prove his point only from the lime shade
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning that leaves lime without a partner also leaves egg membrane without one, so רבי חנינא should have mentioned it too.
